submission.justification:
Radiator-R2 at 3 cm gives the best pion/kaon separation at 10 GeV/c of the three candidates: 4.80 sigma as recorded, with reruns at 4.54 and 4.69 sigma (sim2025 value 4.6). R1 peaks at about 3.7 sigma and R3 at about 2.9 sigma. A thickness scan for R2 peaks near 3.1 cm (fit 4.8 sigma), and 2.5 cm (4.50) and 3.5 cm (4.65) are both lower, so 3 cm is the best grid point within the 1-6 cm range. The transparency constraint, however, is NOT verified. The record shows ageing_transparency_loss_verified = 0 and candidates_eliminated_by_transparency = 0, so no candidate has been shown to meet the 10% maximum transparency loss after the 10-year humidity equivalent. This recommendation is therefore conditional. R2 must pass the humidity ageing test (loss <= 10%) before it is adopted, because it is a hard requirement and the radiator cannot be replaced during the run. If R2 fails, R1 at about 3 cm (3.7 sigma) is the next-best candidate, subject to the same test.</justification>
